us.title: Bartholomae pushes for Spartan Ventures transparency, receives unclear backing from MSU leaders
us.description: Transparency has been a point of contention for Michigan State University's Spartan Ventures since its inception nearly a year ago. This push has come in the form of a new messenger, Athletic Director Dan Bartholomae, yet it is unclear if the administration supports hisquest for transparency. Yesterday, in an interview with The State News, Bartholomae said defining the new name, image and likeness fundraising arm falls under one of three priorities during his first month on the job. "As I've sort of assessed where the challenges are here, I've put them into three buckets: transparency, consistency and competitiveness," Bartholomae said. "The Spartan Ventures piece fits into the transparency bucket." Bartholomae said he doesn't "want to define something that" he is "still learning about."MSU Athletics staff were moved over to Spartan Ventures after the fundraising arm launched on July 1, according to staff directories, but even they "can't explain it," he said. Bartholomae also said to expect "a pretty loud statement" defining Spartan Ventures and its future direction in early 2027 - over a year after the initiation of the entity. Both Board Chair Brianna Scott and President Kevin Guskiewicz sit on the board of Spartan Ventures with Bartholomae. Scott and Guskiewicz did not directly respond to questions asking if Bartholomae's remarks meant a different direction for transparency and instead responded in a joint statement: "(Bartholomae) has made clear that transparency will be a priority as he reviews Spartan Ventures and its role in Michigan State Athletics," the statement read. "We want to give him the opportunity to take a thoughtful, comprehensive look at the program, meet with stakeholders and assess how it can best contribute to our long-term success. We appreciate his deliberate approach and look forward to his recommendations as we continue building a strong future for Spartan Athletics." When first introduced, Spartan Ventures was heavily criticized for the lack of public disclosure. In order to view any operational organizational documents, the MSU Board of Trustees has been asked to sign non-disclosure agreements. Scott and Trustee Sandy Pierce have publicly said they signed the NDA. When the board first approved the initiative in October 2025, former Athletic Director J Batt framed Spartan Ventures as a "competitive advantage." The board laterapproved a spin off, the for-profit company Spartan Media Ventures, at their December 2025 meeting. Trustee Mike Balow drafted a resolution to make Spartan Media Ventures subject to public records requests but did not have enough board support to bring it to a vote during their April meeting.

es.title: No saber disimular
es.description: No me esperaba yo el lunes que unas pocas horas después de levantarme con migraña iba a ver algo en la tele que me sentaría tan bien. Yo estaba en el sofá con mi taza de cereales y el antiinflamatorio que suelo tomar para el dolor. Mientras iba tragando, vi una imagen que me hizo estallar en un ataque de risa. Se me desparramaron los cereales -hecho que mi perro aprovechó en seguida para ponerse las botas- y en seguida paré de comer. La fachada de la sede del PP en Madrid estaba siendo forrada con una gigantesca lona de arriba abajo con el nuevo lema del partido. Me pregunté desde cuándo la tendrían preparada, puesto que ignoro si se puede hacer algo tan grande improvisadamente. A saber desde cuándo estarían rezando los militantes por poder llevar a cabo tal desparrame de ingeniería. ‘Por fin’, decían las letras del cartel. Sí, muy bien elegido el lema, reflejo de la desesperación que los derechistas han ido acumulando durante toda la legislatura.

gr.title: 28η Οκτωβρίου: Τι ισχύει για τις απουσίες στη γιορτή και την παρέλαση – Ποιες δεν μετράνε
gr.description: Τι προβλέπεται για την καταχώριση των απουσιών των μαθητών στις εορταστικές εκδηλώσεις και την παρέλαση για την 28η Οκτωβρίου Με τις σχολικές εκδηλώσεις για την επέτειο της 28ης Οκτωβρίου να πλησιάζουν, μαθητές και εκπαιδευτικοί προετοιμάζονται για τη γιορτή που θα πραγματοποιηθεί στα σχολεία, αλλά και για τις μαθητικές παρελάσεις σε όλη τη χώρα. Ιδιαίτερο ενδιαφέρον παρουσιάζει το τι ισχύει σχετικά με τις απουσίες των μαθητών στην σχολική γιορτή και στις πρόβες της παρέλασης. Για την τρέχουσα σχολική χρονιά, η σχολική γιορτή για την επέτειο της 28ης Οκτωβρίου θα πραγματοποιηθεί παραμονές της εθνικής επετείου ήτοι την Τρίτη 27 Οκτωβρίου, ενώ η Τετάρτη 28 Οκτωβρίου είναι η ημέρα της εθνικής επετείου και αποτελεί σχολική αργία. Στη Θεσσαλονίκη, λόγω της στρατιωτικής παρέλασης που πραγματοποιείται στις 28 Οκτωβρίου, η μαθητική παρέλαση πραγματοποιείται την προηγούμενη ημέρα στις 27 του μήνα και η καθιερωμένη σχολική γιορτή είναι προγραμματισμένη για τις 23 Οκτωβρίου. Η σχολική γιορτή στις 27 Οκτωβρίου: Τι ισχύει για τις απουσίες Η σχολική εκδήλωση για την επέτειο πραγματοποιείται στο πλαίσιο της λειτουργίας της σχολικής μονάδας και η παρουσία των μαθητών είναι υποχρεωτική. Κατά τη διάρκεια της γιορτής τηρείται παρουσιολόγιο, επομένως η απουσία μαθητή καταγράφεται. Στα Γυμνάσια και τα Λύκεια οι εκδηλώσεις πραγματοποιούνται για τουλάχιστον δύο διδακτικές ώρες, ενώ στα Δημοτικά η διάρκεια καθορίζεται από τον διευθυντή ή τη διευθύντρια και τον Σύλλογο Διδασκόντων. Το πρόγραμμα μπορεί να περιλαμβάνει αφηγήσεις, ποιήματα, τραγούδια, θεατρικά δρώμενα και ιστορικές αναφορές στα γεγονότα του 1940. Παράλληλα, πραγματοποιούνται οι προβλεπόμενες διαδικασίες για την παράδοση της σημαίας στους σημαιοφόρους και τους παραστάτες, καθώς και οι απονομές βραβείων και αριστείων. Μετά το τέλος της εκδήλωσης, τα παιδιά αποχωρούν. Το πρωτόκολλο για τις απουσίες για τις πρόβες της παρέλασης Διαφορετικό είναι το καθεστώς για τις πρόβες που πραγματοποιούνται ενόψει της μαθητικής παρέλασης. Οι μαθητές που συμμετέχουν στην παρέλαση ακολουθούν το πρόγραμμα προετοιμασίας που καθορίζει η σχολική μονάδα. Οι απουσίες που προκύπτουν κατά τη διάρκεια των προβών της παρέλασης καταγράφονται μεν αλλά και δεν προσμετρώνται στο σύνολο των απουσιών του μαθητή. Πρόκειται για ειδική ρύθμιση που αφορά τη συμμετοχή των μαθητών στην προετοιμασία της παρέλασης. Η ίδια η 28η Οκτωβρίου αποτελεί ημέρα εθνικής επετείου και σχολική αργία. Τα σχολεία είναι κλειστά και οι μαθητές εφόσον συμμετέχουν στις μαθητικές παρελάσεις καλούνται να δώσουν υποχρεωτικά το παρών. Σε περίπτωση που ένας μαθητής δεν μπορέσει να συμμετάσχει στην παρέλαση εξαιτίας απρόβλεπτου γεγονότος ή λόγου ανωτέρας βίας, δεν τίθεται ζήτημα απουσίας από τα μαθήματα, καθώς εκείνη την ημέρα δεν υπάρχει κανονικό διδακτικό πρόγραμμα. #28Η_ΟΚΤΩΒΡΙΟΥ #ΣΧΟΛΕΙΑ #ΑΠΟΥΣΙΕΣ #ΜΑΘΗΤΙΚΗ_ΠΑΡΕΛΑΣΗ #ΠΑΡΕΛΑΣΗ #ΣΧΟΛΙΚΗ_ΓΙΟΡΤΗ

vn.title: AIRA Factoring vượt mốc 1 tỷ THB về tài trợ chuỗi cung ứng số với sự hỗ trợ của NEC Thailand
vn.description: BANGKOK, ngày 9 tháng 10 năm 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AIRA Factoring Public Company Limited đã đạt một cột mốc quan trọng trong quá trình chuyển đổi số khi vượt mốc 1 tỷ THB về tổng giá trị các giao dịch cho vay lũy kế thông qua nền tảng tài trợ chuỗi cung ứng số tiên tiến trong thời gian kỷ lục. Nền tảng được phát triển với sự hợp tác của NEC Thailand và TASConnect. Bằng việc số hóa các quy trình vốn lưu động, nền tảng này cung cấp cho các doanh nghiệp khả năng thanh khoản nhanh chóng, nâng cao khả năng theo dõi dòng tiền và giảm các trở ngại trong vận hành. Nền tảng giúp bên mua, nhà cung cấp và các tổ chức tài chính xây dựng chuỗi cung ứng có khả năng chống chịu, đồng thời tích hợp các chỉ số ESG vào các khuôn khổ tài chính bền vững. Nền tảng này tạo điều kiện cho chuyển đổi trong hoạt động tài trợ chuỗi cung ứng thông qua một hệ sinh thái kết nối linh hoạt, dựa trên dữ liệu. "Cột mốc 1 tỷ THB này phản ánh sự tin tưởng của khách hàng, nhà cung cấp và các đối tác chiến lược của chúng tôi", Ông Akrawit Sooksai, Giám đốc Điều hành của AIRA Factoring Public Company Limited cho biết. "Tài trợ chuỗi cung ứng số đã phát triển từ một sáng kiến công nghệ thành động lực tăng trưởng kinh doanh thực sự — giúp các công ty củng cố thanh khoản và nắm bắt những cơ hội thị trường mới. Khi mức độ ứng dụng ngày càng tăng, chúng tôi dự đoán hoạt động này sẽ tiếp tục mở rộng với mức tăng trưởng khoảng 7%". Cùng kiến tạo giá trị xã hội và kinh tế cho Thái Lan Trong nhiều thập kỷ, NEC Thailand đã phát triển đồng hành cùng xã hội Thái Lan với vai trò là đối tác công nghệ đáng tin cậy, chuyên giải quyết những thách thức phức tạp trong kinh doanh và xã hội. "Cam kết của NEC không chỉ dừng lại ở việc triển khai công nghệ — chúng tôi tập trung vào việc cùng kiến tạo những giá trị lâu dài cho xã hội", Ông Hiroki Yoshifuji, Chủ tịch NEC Corporation (Thailand) Ltd. cho biết. "Bằng việc cung cấp một nền tảng tài trợ chuỗi cung ứng số có tính bảo mật cao và đáng tin cậy, chúng tôi đang giúp các doanh nghiệp địa phương và doanh nghiệp vừa và nhỏ (SME) tiếp cận nguồn vốn kịp thời. Việc củng cố thanh khoản tài chính trong toàn chuỗi cung ứng góp phần xây dựng nền tảng kinh tế có khả năng chống chịu tốt hơn cho Thái Lan, thúc đẩy tăng trưởng bền vững cho cả doanh nghiệp và xã hội". Thành tựu mang tính cột mốc này sẽ được nêu bật tại Digital Converge 2026, cho thấy sự phối hợp giữa AIRA Factoring, NEC Thailand và TASConnect đang thiết lập một chuẩn mực mới về mức độ phát triển của chuỗi cung ứng số trong khu vực. Về tổng thể, nền tảng này mang lại những tác động có thể đo lường đối với doanh nghiệp thông qua việc đẩy nhanh dòng vốn cho các nhà cung cấp, nâng cao tính minh bạch xuyên suốt chuỗi cung ứng và tích hợp các nguyên tắc ESG vào hoạt động tài trợ vốn cho doanh nghiệp. Được xây dựng trên kiến trúc có khả năng mở rộng, đạt tiêu chuẩn doanh nghiệp của NEC, giải pháp giảm thiểu rủi ro vận hành, đồng thời cung cấp một nền tảng đã được chứng minh và sẵn sàng cho tương lai để tăng trưởng kinh doanh liên tục và mở rộng trong khu vực.

vn.title: UOB Asset Management nhấn mạnh các cơ hội trong bối cảnh chính sách toàn cầu thay đổi
vn.description: SINGAPORE, ngày 9 tháng 10 năm 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- UOB Asset Management (UOBAM) đã công bố Chiến lược Đầu tư Quý 4 năm 2026, nhấn mạnh rằng chính sách tiền tệ đang thay đổi, các nền tảng kinh tế vững vàng và những xu hướng tăng trưởng mang tính cấu trúc tiếp tục tạo ra cơ hội cho các nhà đầu tư bất chấp bối cảnh toàn cầu đầy bất ổn. Trong bối cảnh thị trường tài chính đang ứng phó với giai đoạn bất ổn chính sách gia tăng, nền kinh tế toàn cầu nhìn chung vẫn duy trì khả năng chống chịu tốt. Hoạt động kinh tế tại các khu vực lớn tiếp tục mở rộng, lợi nhuận doanh nghiệp tiếp tục là yếu tố hỗ trợ, và các khoản đầu tư vào các công nghệ mang tính chuyển đổi như trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI) tiếp tục làm nền tảng cho triển vọng tăng trưởng dài hạn. Trong khi các nhà đầu tư tiếp tục phải đối mặt với những diễn biến địa chính trị, thay đổi trong chính sách thương mại và những vấn đề xoay quanh triển vọng lãi suất, UOBAM tin rằng biến động thị trường nên được nhìn nhận như một cơ hội để các nhà đầu tư có kỷ luật chuẩn bị vị thế nhằm hướng tới mức sinh lời hấp dẫn trong dài hạn. Về lãi suất, UOBAM không kỳ vọng sẽ xảy ra một chu kỳ tăng lãi suất mạnh hoặc lợi suất trái phiếu tiếp tục tăng mạnh, khi nhiều yếu tố thúc đẩy áp lực giá cả đang cho thấy dấu hiệu hạ nhiệt. Đối với cổ phiếu, UOBAM tiếp tục duy trì quan điểm tích cực, với ưu tiên dành cho thị trường Hoa Kỳ và Châu Á. Hoa Kỳ tiếp tục mang đến sự kết hợp hấp dẫn giữa tăng trưởng lợi nhuận, đổi mới và độ sâu thị trường. Trong khi đó, Châu Á sở hữu các nền tảng dài hạn hấp dẫn, được hỗ trợ bởi tăng trưởng kinh tế mạnh mẽ hơn, định giá hấp dẫn và vị thế dẫn đầu trong các ngành như bán dẫn, bộ nhớ, năng lượng thay thế và xe điện. Ông Anthony Raza, Trưởng bộ phận Chiến lược Đa tài sản của UOBAM, cho biết: "Điểm đáng chú ý đối với các nhà đầu tư là nền kinh tế toàn cầu vẫn duy trì sức mạnh bất chấp liên tiếp phải đối mặt với các yếu tố bất lợi. Rất khó tìm thấy một giai đoạn nào trong lịch sử mà tăng trưởng lợi nhuận doanh nghiệp toàn cầu lại mạnh mẽ như hiện nay, đặc biệt khi chu kỳ mở rộng kinh tế đã kéo dài đến giai đoạn này. Tuy nhiên, chu kỳ kinh tế đang cho thấy những dấu hiệu điển hình của giai đoạn cuối chu kỳ. Xét cho cùng, mặc dù những dấu hiệu cuối chu kỳ hiện nay cần được theo dõi, chúng tôi tin rằng vẫn còn quá sớm để từ bỏ chiến lược đầu tư định hướng tăng trưởng". Trong chiến lược phân bổ tài sản, UOBAM tiếp tục duy trì tăng tỷ trọng cổ phiếu và giảm tỷ trọng tài sản thu nhập cố định. Công ty tiếp tục duy trì triển vọng tích cực đối với hàng hóa và xem vàng là một nguồn đa dạng hóa danh mục đầu tư quan trọng. Để có thêm thông tin chuyên sâu về cổ phiếu, tài sản thu nhập cố định, tiền tệ và hàng hóa, vui lòng đọc toàn bộ Chiến lược Đầu tư Quý 4 năm 2026 tại: https://www.uobam.com.sg/insights/quarterly-investment-strategy/qis4q26.page Giới thiệu về UOB Asset Management UOB Asset Management Ltd (UOBAM) là công ty con thuộc sở hữu hoàn toàn của United Overseas Bank Limited. Được thành lập vào năm 1986, UOBAM có 40 năm kinh nghiệm trong việc quản lý các chương trình đầu tư tập thể và các quỹ đầu tư ủy thác toàn quyền. Tính đến ngày 31 tháng 8 năm 2026, UOBAM quản lý 63 quỹ tín thác tại Singapore và cùng với các công ty con, giám sát 43,9 tỷ đô la Singapore tài sản quản lý. Mạng lưới của công ty bao gồm UOB Islamic Asset Management Sdn Bhd tại Malaysia, liên doanh với Ping An Fund Management Company Limited tại Trung Quốc, cùng liên minh chiến lược với các đối tác đầu tư toàn cầu. in.title: AIRA Factoring Surpasses THB 1 Billion in Digital Supply Chain Financing, Powered by NEC Thailand
in.description: BANGKOK, Oct. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AIRA Factoring Public Company Limited has achieved a major digital transformation milestone, exceeding THB 1 Billion in cumulative lending transactions through its advanced digital supply chain financing platform in record time. Developed in collaboration with NEC Thailand and TASConnect. By digitizing working capital workflows, the platform provides businesses with rapid liquidity, enhanced cash flow visibility, and reduced operational friction. It empowers buyers, suppliers, and financial institutions to build resilient supply chains while integrating ESG metrics into sustainable financing frameworks. The platform facilitates transformation in supply chain financing through an agile, data-driven connected ecosystem. "This THB 1 Billion milestone reflects the trust of our customers, suppliers, and strategic partners," stated Mr. Akrawit Sooksai, Chief Executive Officer of AIRA Factoring Public Company Limited. "Digital supply chain financing has evolved from a technology initiative into a true business growth engine—enabling companies to strengthen liquidity and capture new market opportunities. As adoption accelerates, we anticipate continued expansion with approximately 7% growth." Co-Creating Social & Economic Value for Thailand For decades, NEC Thailand has grown alongside Thai society as a trusted technology partner dedicated to solving complex business and societal challenges. "At NEC, our commitment goes beyond technology deployment—we focus on co-creating lasting value for society," said Mr. Hiroki Yoshifuji, President of NEC Corporation (Thailand) Ltd."By delivering a highly secure, reliable digital supply chain finance platform, we are empowering local businesses and SMEs with timely access to capital. Strengthening financial liquidity across the supply chain builds a more resilient economic foundation for Thailand, driving sustainable growth for enterprises and society alike." This milestone achievement will be highlighted at Digital Converge 2026, demonstrating how the synergy among AIRA Factoring, NEC Thailand, and TASConnect is setting a new benchmark for digital supply chain maturity across the region. Ultimately, the platform delivers measurable enterprise impact by accelerating capital flow for suppliers, enhancing end-to-end supply chain transparency, and embedding ESG principles into corporate financing. Built on NEC's enterprise-grade, scalable architecture, the solution mitigates operational risk while providing a proven, future-ready foundation for continuous business growth and regional expansion.

in.title: UOB Asset Management Highlights Opportunities Amid Shifting Global Policy Landscape
in.description: SINGAPORE, Oct. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- UOB Asset Management (UOBAM) has released its 4Q 2026 Quarterly Investment Strategy, highlighting how evolving monetary policy, resilient economic fundamentals and structural growth trends continue to create opportunities for investors despite an uncertain global backdrop. As financial markets navigate a period of heightened policy uncertainty, the global economy has remained broadly resilient. Economic activity across major regions has continued to expand, corporate earnings have remained supportive, and investments in transformational technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) continue to underpin long-term growth prospects. While investors continue to contend with geopolitical developments, trade policy changes and questions surrounding the outlook for interest rates, UOBAM believes that market volatility should be viewed as an opportunity for disciplined investors to position for attractive long-term returns. On interest rates, UOBAM does not expect an aggressive rate hiking cycle or bond yields to continue surging higher as many of the factors driving price pressures are showing signs of moderation. Within equities, UOBAM remains positive, with a preference for the US and Asia. The US continues to offer a compelling combination of earnings growth, innovation and market depth. Asia, meanwhile, offers attractive long-term fundamentals, supported by stronger economic growth, compelling valuations and leadership positions in industries such as semiconductors, memory, alternative energy and electric vehicles. Anthony Raza, Head of UOBAM Multi-Asset Strategy, said, "The key story for investors is that the global economy has stayed strong despite a constant stream of headwinds. It is hard to find a period in history when global corporate earnings growth has been as strong as it is today, especially this far into an economic expansion. However, the economic cycle is showing classic late-cycle signs. Ultimately, while today's late-cycle signals warrant monitoring, we believe it remains too early to step away from a growth-oriented investment strategy." In its asset allocation strategy, UOBAM remains overweight equities and underweight fixed income. The firm continues to retain a positive outlook on commodities and views gold as an important source of portfolio diversification. For deeper insights across equities, fixed income, currencies and commodities, read the full 4Q 2026 Investment Strategy: https://www.uobam.com.sg/insights/quarterly-investment-strategy/qis4q26.page About UOB Asset Management UOB Asset Management Ltd (UOBAM) is a wholly owned subsidiary of United Overseas Bank Limited. Established in 1986, UOBAM has 40 years of experience managing collective investment schemes and discretionary funds. As at 31 August 2026, UOBAM manages 63 unit trusts in Singapore and together with its subsidiaries, oversees S$43.9 billion in assets under management. Headquartered in Singapore, UOBAM has business and investment offices across Brunei, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam. Its network includes UOB Islamic Asset Management Sdn Bhd in Malaysia, a joint venture with Ping An Fund Management Company Limited in China, and strategic alliances with global investment partners. UOBAM has received more than 400 industry awards for its investment, digital and sustainable investing capabilities. Its 2026 accolades include Most Innovative Application of Artificial Intelligence (ASEAN)[1], received for the third consecutive year, and the Most Innovative Product (Singapore)[1], alongside investment and sustainability awards across its regional markets. UOBAM was also named Best Regional Asset Management Company in 2025[1] and Best Asset Management House in Asia - 20 Years in 2023[1]. ae.title: UOB Asset Management Highlights Opportunities Amid Shifting Global Policy Landscape
ae.description: SINGAPORE, Oct. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- UOB Asset Management (UOBAM) has released its 4Q 2026 Quarterly Investment Strategy, highlighting how evolving monetary policy, resilient economic fundamentals and structural growth trends continue to create opportunities for investors despite an uncertain global backdrop. As financial markets navigate a period of heightened policy uncertainty, the global economy has remained broadly resilient. Economic activity across major regions has continued to expand, corporate earnings have remained supportive, and investments in transformational technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) continue to underpin long-term growth prospects. While investors continue to contend with geopolitical developments, trade policy changes and questions surrounding the outlook for interest rates, UOBAM believes that market volatility should be viewed as an opportunity for disciplined investors to position for attractive long-term returns. On interest rates, UOBAM does not expect an aggressive rate hiking cycle or bond yields to continue surging higher as many of the factors driving price pressures are showing signs of moderation. Within equities, UOBAM remains positive, with a preference for the US and Asia. The US continues to offer a compelling combination of earnings growth, innovation and market depth. Asia, meanwhile, offers attractive long-term fundamentals, supported by stronger economic growth, compelling valuations and leadership positions in industries such as semiconductors, memory, alternative energy and electric vehicles. Anthony Raza, Head of UOBAM Multi-Asset Strategy, said, "The key story for investors is that the global economy has stayed strong despite a constant stream of headwinds. It is hard to find a period in history when global corporate earnings growth has been as strong as it is today, especially this far into an economic expansion. However, the economic cycle is showing classic late-cycle signs. Ultimately, while today's late-cycle signals warrant monitoring, we believe it remains too early to step away from a growth-oriented investment strategy." In its asset allocation strategy, UOBAM remains overweight equities and underweight fixed income. The firm continues to retain a positive outlook on commodities and views gold as an important source of portfolio diversification. ae.title: UAE private schools: How a three-tier AI model is helping identify and support students with academic difficulties
ae.description: Abu Dhabi: Private schools across the country have activated the ‘Academic Difficulties’ indicator to provide a proactive response by employing artificial intelligence technologies to analyse data and identify students facing learning challenges. This is based on a set of evidence-based factors and criteria, helping to understand their needs and guide appropriate intervention and support using tiered intervention models. These models begin with in-class support and progress to more specialised interventions tailored to the student's individual needs. The factors include academic achievement, behaviour, language difficulties, additional educational needs, and circumstances affecting the student or their family, in addition to assessments, referrals, and parental involvement. In detail, private schools have confirmed the activation of a data-driven system with continuous monitoring, combining educational assessment tools, the professional expertise of teachers and support teams, and the use of artificial intelligence technologies to analyse indicators and identify educational needs. They emphasised the importance of partnership with families in understanding the factors affecting student learning, monitoring the effectiveness of interventions, and refining them based on the student's response and progress. Three-tiered model In letters sent to students' families, the Ministry outlined a three-tiered model to support students facing academic difficulties. The first tier focuses on comprehensive, evidence-based instruction provided to all students in the classroom, emphasising building positive relationships and creating a supportive environment. Student progress is continuously monitored, and those who do not respond to interventions at this level are moved to the next level for additional instruction to achieve their academic and behavioural goals. The third level of intervention is the ‘intensive level’, which focuses on specialised, individualised instruction requiring tailored intervention to the student's specific needs and may include assistance from external specialists. The schools emphasised the importance of developing intervention programs using a comprehensive, structured, and phased approach. This approach is based on assessing the underlying factors that led to a student being considered at risk of academic difficulty. It aims to comprehensively address the needs of these students through collaboration between school and home, adopting a holistic approach within the school that seeks supportive improvement in both contexts, implementing high-quality intervention programs grounded in culturally and linguistically relevant research, and employing adaptive teaching to support inclusion. The approach reinforces the principle that every student has the capacity to learn and reach their full potential. Cooperative families The schools explained that the elements of the intervention program for students at risk of academic difficulty also include integrating an evidence-based data collection and assessment system, including comprehensive and diagnostic screening, and monitoring progress to guide decision-making at each level of support. This system utilises problem-solving techniques to develop individualised learning plans, employs a research-based positive behavioural approach in the school and classroom to support academic achievement and psychosocial learning, and implements a collaborative approach to analysing student data and coordinating the intervention process. The schools urged families to cooperate in monitoring any indicators or signs that might suggest academic difficulties in their children, and to share any relevant observations or information that could contribute to understanding the student's needs and the factors affecting their educational progress. They emphasised that effective partnership between the school and the family is essential for the early detection of educational challenges and helps in taking appropriate measures in a timely manner, ensuring the provision of support and interventions tailored to the student's needs, and the continuous monitoring of their academic and behavioural development. Adnan Abbas, Executive Director of Al Nahda National Schools in Abu Dhabi, affirmed that academic difficulty monitoring programs are an important tool for identifying challenges students may face early on. He explained that "their goal is not limited to identifying weaknesses in academic achievement, but extends to understanding the reasons and factors affecting the student's progress, whether they are academic, behavioural, social, or related to additional educational needs." He said, “These programs allow the school to intervene promptly and develop support plans tailored to each student’s needs, rather than waiting until difficulties worsen and negatively impact their academic performance, self-confidence, and motivation to learn. Furthermore, these educational interventions will be supported by artificial intelligence, as schools are developing and implementing technological programs and solutions that enable them to analyse data more effectively, understand students’ needs, and tailor educational interventions to each student’s specific requirements. This will enhance the school’s ability to provide more precise and responsive support.” He emphasised that the effectiveness of these programs depends on a genuine partnership between the school and the family, along with continuous monitoring of the student’s response to the interventions. He affirmed that the data and observations collected by the school are used to guide educational decisions and develop support plans, not to create fixed classifications for students. Interventions are tiered according to the student’s level of need, ranging from in-class support for all students to specialised and intensive interventions when necessary. Parents are involved in the monitoring and evaluation stages, in developing the support plan, and in tracking the student’s progress. Meeting students' needs Educational consultant Shereen Farag emphasised the importance of having an early detection system for academic difficulties, "because it helps us understand the student's needs before the educational gap widens, and thus support can be provided in a timely and appropriate manner." She added: "The earlier the intervention, the greater the student's chances of regaining their academic progress and maintaining their self-confidence and motivation to learn, especially since academic difficulties do not occur suddenly, but are often preceded by a set of indicators that can be detected early, whether through assessment results, class participation, achievement level, or changes in motivation, behaviour, and interaction with learning. Most importantly, the goal of monitoring is not to classify the student or place them in a failing category, but rather to understand what they need so that we can help them succeed." She continued: “Gradual intervention models are among the most effective practices in addressing students’ needs because they begin in the classroom and with the teacher’s daily practices. If follow-up shows that the student needs deeper support, the school moves to a more focused level of intervention. What distinguishes this model is that it doesn’t wait for the student to reach an advanced stage of difficulty, but rather relies on continuous monitoring and measuring the impact of the intervention, then adjusting the level of support based on the student’s response. This makes educational decisions more flexible and accurate.” She explained that the real contribution that artificial intelligence can make to the monitoring and follow-up process lies in its ability to analyse large amounts of data and link a range of indicators simultaneously, such as academic achievement, assessment results, attendance, participation, and progress patterns. This helps schools detect certain patterns or risk indicators at an early stage and gives teachers and support teams a more comprehensive picture of the student. She pointed out that artificial intelligence in schools is a tool to support educational decision-making, not a replacement for the teacher or professional judgment. She stressed that parents are key partners in the success of the student support system, because they contribute to providing a more comprehensive picture of the student’s needs and the factors that may affect his learning. Continuous communication between the family and the school helps to unify efforts and follow up on the support plan more effectively. The more the parent is a partner in understanding the student’s needs and following up on his progress, the more consistent and sustainable the interventions become, and this is reflected positively on the student’s progress and motivation to learn.

ae.title: UAE mid-term break travel 2026: Holiday bookings jump 31%, with Maldives, Spain and France topping the list
ae.description: Dubai: The latest booking data from dnata Travel reveals a significant increase in holiday bookings in the UAE during the mid-term break in October, jumping by 31% compared to last year, reflecting the growing demand for holidays, particularly in nearby destinations. The UAE topped the list of preferred destinations for citizens and residents to spend school holidays, and travel abroad also maintained its strong momentum, with the Maldives, Spain, France, Thailand and Mauritius topping the list of the most popular overseas destinations. In the UAE, Dubai accounted for 78% of holiday accommodation bookings, followed by Abu Dhabi and Ras Al Khaimah. Booking trends showed strong demand for hotels that offer easy access to entertainment, leisure and lifestyle experiences, including hotels and resorts on Palm Jumeirah, beach resorts and Yas Island. As for international destinations, Spain saw a 65% increase in bookings compared to last year, while demand for travel to the United States rose by 6%. Bookings in France and Japan also saw significant growth compared to last year's levels, and Finland recorded increasing interest among travellers seeking cold-weather experiences. Bookings through dnata Travel's retail stores rose by 16%, while bookings through social media channels tripled compared to last year, coinciding with a rise in spending on family travel, as average booking values recorded a 6% year-on-year increase. Mira Kititt, Head of Retail and Leisure in the UAE at dnata Travel, said: “The mid-term break in October is an important period for local and international holidays for citizens and residents of the UAE, and the growing popularity of local holidays reflects one of the most prominent shifts in this field, as families place greater value on comfort, flexibility and meaningful experiences, with short breaks becoming increasingly popular as an attractive way to make the most of holidays.” She added: “Data on holiday bookings outside the UAE showed strong demand for nearby beach destinations such as the Maldives, Mauritius, and Thailand, as these destinations continued to attract travellers by offering a mix of benefits, such as easy access and attractive value for family holidays. We also noted the growing role of social media in inspiring travel destination choices and shaping booking decisions.” Dnata Travel has launched offers during the mid-term break for a one-night stay at the five-star Hilton Dubai Palm Jumeirah Hotel, including breakfast and free accommodation for one child up to the age of 11, with prices starting from Dh545 per person. It also offered a one-night stay in a family suite with a view of the plaza at the four-star Yas Plaza Hotel, including breakfast, tickets to theme parks and free accommodation for two children up to the age of 11, with prices starting from Dh545 per person. Dnata Travel’s offers included a one-night stay in a Deluxe King Room with a sea view at the five-star Le Méridien Al Aqah Beach Resort, including breakfast, with prices starting from Dh695 per person. As for the international destination offers, they include a three-night stay in a double room at the five-star Hilton Helsinki Strand Hotel in Finland, including breakfast and round-trip airfare, with prices starting from Dh4,035 per person. Dnata Travel also offered a three-night stay in a large beach villa with a swimming pool at the five-star Sun Siam Olhuveli resort in the Maldives. The offer includes all meals, transfers, accommodation, and free meals for children. It also allows you to enjoy savings of 30% on accommodation, 50% on round-trip speedboat transfers, and a free Lucky Dolphin cruise. It also includes round-trip airfare, with prices starting from Dh7,420 per person. As for the Mauritius offer, it includes a three-night stay in a Prestige Room at the five-star Sea Mauritius Hotel, including breakfast and dinner, with savings of up to 40% on accommodation and round-trip airfare, with prices starting from Dh6,590 per person.

UAE expands cultural and creative industries ecosystem
ae.description: Abu Dhabi: The UAE is moving to establish culture and creativity as fully integrated economic sectors, connected to production, financing, intellectual property rights, distribution, and markets, and bringing together talent, projects, products, and audiences. The initiatives and achievements witnessed across the country in 2026 reflect the growing scope of the cultural and creative industries ecosystem, spanning publishing, film, gaming, design, content production, financing programmes, and talent development. Together, these efforts are supporting the growth of new products, markets, and business opportunities within the creative economy. In this context, Dubai retained its position as the world’s leading destination for attracting new foreign direct investment (FDI) projects in the cultural and creative industries for the fourth consecutive year in 2025. The emirate attracted 754 projects, generating total capital investment flows of $3.756 billion and creating more than 19,300 new jobs. The projects covered advertising and public relations, programming and digital services, film and media production, electronic gaming, creative technology, education, design, and architecture. The publishing sector provides a clear example of this expansion. The 35th edition of the Abu Dhabi International Book Fair brought together 1,200 exhibitors from 95 countries, including seven countries participating for the first time, alongside around 1,500 events. Its professional programme explored the future of books, intellectual property, publishing and translation rights, as well as changes in reader behaviour and market trends. On the first day of the fair, the value of book sales increased by 97%, the number of books sold rose by 108%, visitor numbers grew by 11%, and total sales increased by 93%, compared with the same period in 2025. The publishing sector is also expanding beyond book fairs into distribution, rights, and markets. Menassah Distribution made 1,004 titles from 75 UAE-based publishing houses available, representing a total of 8,500 books during the 2026 Abu Dhabi International Book Fair. Meanwhile, the National Media Authority announced that more than 100,000 permits were issued for the circulation of books and publications in the UAE during 2025, alongside the processing of nearly 1.2 million titles entering the country through its various points of entry. At the same time, studies conducted by Sharjah Publishing City (SPC) indicate that the UAE’s publishing industry market is projected to grow from $260 million to $650 million by 2030. The UAE’s cinema sector, meanwhile, generated box-office revenues exceeding AED 734 million in 2025, with more than 14.8 million tickets sold for approximately 1,270 films, according to the National Media Authority. In digital gaming, revenues reached AED 2.7 billion, while the number of games reviewed and classified rose to 552, compared with 375 in 2024. This reflects the expanding range of creative activities associated with digital content. The growth of the creative economy has also extended to the design sector, with Dubai adopting the "Dubai Design Sector Strategy 2033” to develop the industry and strengthen its competitiveness. The strategy aims to increase enrolment in higher education and continuing professional training in design by 20%, provide opportunities for more than 25,000 students, support around 500 existing projects, incubate more than 100 new projects, showcase more than 500 local projects at international exhibitions and events, organise more than 100 events, and attract four million local and international visitors by 2033. It covers fashion, product design, architecture, and graphic design, while also facilitating business formation and access to financing. Investment in creativity also extends to content production. Dubai Culture launched the "Stories of Wulfa”” competition to produce an animated series inspired by Emirati culture, values, and traditions. The initiative provides AED 2 million in funding for development, production, and distribution, and is open to artists, writers, illustrators, directors, designers, filmmakers, animation studios, and production companies. The growth of the creative economy is not limited to developing markets and products; it is also expanding to support production and talent through government funding and grant programmes. The Ministry of Culture announced the launch of the fifth cycle of the National Grant Programme for Culture and Creativity, which aims to support Emirati creatives and enable them to develop cultural and creative projects, thereby strengthening cultural production and the growth of the country’s creative industries. The programme provides support to creatives across four main categories: creativity and production; distribution and local participation; skills development; and international travel and mobility. These categories cover fields including writing and publishing, music, film and television, performing arts and theatre, visual arts and design, video games, and cultural heritage. In March, the Ministry of Culture also announced a new cycle of the 2026 Cultural Public Benefit Associations Subsidies and Grants Programme. The initiative aims to strengthen the role of cultural associations and artistic groups and enable them to implement high-quality projects that contribute to national identity, create new platforms for talent, and broaden cultural participation across the UAE’s emirates. The programme provides grants for innovative projects aligned with associations’ plans in areas including cultural festivals, cultural education, creative production, and international participation, as well as literature and the Arabic language, music, film and cinema, cultural heritage and national identity, design and architecture, visual and digital arts, animation and electronic gaming, and culinary arts.

ml.title: Dr Seydou Diallo : « Nous avons dépassé le seuil de 70% de dépistage »
ml.description: © Internet Chef du service de santé mère-enfant à l’Office national de la santé de la reproduction (ONASR), le Dr Seydou Diallo revient sur les efforts engagés dans le dépistage des cancers du sein et du col de l’utérus. Il évoque la progression du recours au dépistage, les difficultés persistantes dans certaines zones et le dispositif de prise en charge mis en place au CHU du Point G. Propos recueillis par Mohamed Kenouvi Quel bilan l’ONASR dresse-t-il aujourd’hui du dépistage des cancers du sein et du col de l’utérus ? Le bilan que nous dressons aujourd’hui est vraiment élogieux. Avec l’opérationnalisation de l’ONASR en 2022, nous avons commencé à organiser régulièrement, chaque année, Octobre Rose, consacré au dépistage du cancer du sein, que nous avons associé au dépistage du cancer du col de l’utérus. En outre, le dépistage est intégré à la campagne de planification familiale, désormais couplée au dépistage des cancers du col de l’utérus et du sein. Il y a également le programme « Week-end 70 », qui permet d’effectuer le dépistage de routine. Avant l’opérationnalisation de l’ONASR, le taux de dépistage au Mali était inférieur à 5%.Aujourd’hui, nous avons dépassé le seuil de 70%. Cette multiplication des campagnes a-t-elle permis de faire reculer les diagnostics tardifs ? La sensibilisation commence à porter ses fruits. Auparavant, les cancers étaient détectés beaucoup plus tardivement. Aujourd’hui, avec l’augmentation du dépistage, nous constatons que les femmes arrivent moins souvent à des stades avancés, notamment dans le cas du cancer du col de l’utérus. On ne peut pas inverser la tendance d’un seul coup. Cela se fera progressivement, grâce à la sensibilisation et au dépistage précoce. Les difficultés demeurent surtout dans certaines zones humanitaires, où la situation sécuritaire complique l’accès des services de santé aux populations. Malgré cela, des campagnes de sensibilisation et de dépistage y sont également organisées. Qu’en est-il de l’orientation et du suivi des femmes après le dépistage ? Aujourd’hui, il y a moins de difficultés en matière d’orientation. Les femmes chez lesquelles un cancer est confirmé sont orientées vers le CHU du Point G, où existe une chaîne de prise en charge allant du bilan à la chimiothérapie et à la radiothérapie. Un partenariat entre l’État malien et Médecins sans frontières permet aux femmes intégrées dans cette cohorte de bénéficier d’une prise en charge gratuite. Cela concerne le bilan diagnostique, le bilan thérapeutique, la chimiothérapie, la radiothérapie et même l’hormonothérapie. Auparavant, nous ne disposions pas de cette orientation claire et toute la prise en charge était à la charge de la patiente. Aujourd’hui, il faut reconnaître qu’il y a eu une avancée significative. Comment assurer la continuité entre le dépistage, la confirmation du diagnostic et le traitement ? Pour le cancer du col de l’utérus, nous effectuons notamment le dépistage à l’aide des tests IVA/IVL dans nos structures. Pour le cancer du sein, nous encourageons les femmes à pratiquer régulièrement l’autopalpation, notamment après les menstruations, afin de rechercher une asymétrie, une grosseur anormale, une plaie ou une boule. Lorsqu’on veut aller plus loin, la mammographie permet de dépister le cancer du sein. Après le dépistage, la biopsie et l’examen anatomopathologique permettent de confirmer la présence de cellules cancéreuses. Une fois le diagnostic confirmé, les femmes sont orientées vers le CHU du Point G et intégrées dans la cohorte. À partir de là, la prise en charge devient gratuite, du bilan aux traitements. C’est cette chaîne qui permet aujourd’hui d’améliorer la continuité entre le dépistage, le diagnostic et la prise en charge.

ml.title: Aguelhoc : des coupons alimentaires pour 8 000 personnes
ml.description: © Internet Le PAM a commencé les distributions au début de septembre. La première phase couvre environ 1 500 ménages déplacés ou accueillant des familles. Près de 8 000 personnes ont bénéficié d’une première distribution de coupons alimentaires à Aguelhoc, dans la région de Kidal. Selon Aline Samu Nkuelo, représentante et directrice du Programme alimentaire mondial au Mali, l’opération a commencé au début du mois de septembre et concerne environ 1 500 ménages. L’assistance cible des personnes déplacées ainsi que les familles qui les accueillent. Les bénéficiaires utilisent leurs coupons pour acheter des produits alimentaires auprès de commerçants locaux, en fonction des besoins de leur foyer. Ces informations ont été données par la responsable du PAM au cours d’un entretien diffusé le 6 octobre par Studio Tamani. La communication publiée ne précise pas la valeur de chaque coupon, la liste des produits admissibles ou le nombre de commerces participant au dispositif. Une évaluation menée auprès des ménages Avant le lancement de l’opération, le PAM, ses partenaires et d’autres agences ont réalisé une évaluation multisectorielle dans la zone. D’après Aline Samu Nkuelo, trois ménages interrogés sur quatre ont déclaré rencontrer de grandes difficultés pour se nourrir convenablement. La même évaluation a relevé que 99 % des ménages interrogés signalaient une forte baisse de leur pouvoir d’achat. Ce pourcentage concerne les personnes couvertes par l’enquête menée à Aguelhoc. Il ne constitue pas une estimation applicable à l’ensemble des ménages maliens. La responsable du PAM explique que les familles d’accueil partagent leurs ressources avec les nouveaux arrivants. L’opération les intègre donc au dispositif au même titre que les ménages déplacés. Les femmes enceintes ou allaitantes et les jeunes enfants font l’objet d’une attention particulière. Le PAM rattache cette priorité aux niveaux de malnutrition observés dans le nord du pays et aux besoins nutritionnels propres à ces groupes. Des achats auprès des commerçants locaux Le coupon diffère d’une distribution directe de céréales ou d’autres denrées. Il permet au ménage de choisir les produits disponibles auprès des commerçants agréés dans la localité. Ce mécanisme suppose que les marchés disposent de stocks suffisants et que les prix restent suivis pendant l’opération. Il nécessite également un contrôle des coupons remis, des transactions réalisées et des remboursements dus aux commerçants. Le montant attribué à chaque ménage constitue une donnée importante pour apprécier la couverture réelle de l’aide. La communication diffusée le 6 octobre indique le nombre de personnes et de foyers bénéficiaires, mais ne fournit pas cette valeur financière. Aline Samu Nkuelo précise que l’intervention a été préparée avec les autorités maliennes, les responsables communautaires, les organisations non gouvernementales partenaires et les autres agences présentes dans la zone. Une aide nationale fortement ciblée À l’échelle nationale, le PAM estime que plus de 1,5 million de personnes ont été confrontées à une insécurité alimentaire aiguë pendant la période de soudure de juin à août 2026. Une évaluation d’urgence réalisée en juin avait conclu que 40 % des ménages interrogés avaient besoin d’une assistance humanitaire, tandis que 4 % déclaraient en avoir reçu au cours des trois mois précédents. Le PAM indique également que ses difficultés de financement l’ont conduit à réduire la durée de certaines aides de six à trois mois en 2026. Selon l’organisation, plus de 200 000 personnes vulnérables ont été retirées des programmes d’assistance à la suite de cette révision des priorités. À Aguelhoc, le PAM prévoit un suivi après les distributions et la collecte d’avis auprès des bénéficiaires. Aline Samu Nkuelo a indiqué qu’une première observation des effets de l’aide demanderait un à deux mois. Le bilan disponible porte sur le démarrage de l’opération. Il établit que près de 8 000 personnes, réparties dans environ 1 500 ménages, ont reçu des coupons utilisables auprès de commerçants locaux. Les résultats nutritionnels et la durée effective de la prise en charge seront documentés par le suivi annoncé par le PAM. Massiré Diop

A nova estimativa representa uma alteração substancial das perspectivas da instituição para Angola: ainda em Junho, no Global Economic Prospects, projectava uma expansão de apenas 2,4%. A diferença é de 2,1 pontos percentuais.

ao.title: O EXPLICADOR FISCAL: Mercado monetário interbancário (MMI) imposto do selo
ao.description: O Banco XPTO realiza regularmente operações no Mercado Monetário Interbancário (MMI) com maturidades inferiores a cinco dias, as quais beneficiam de isenção de Imposto do Selo. Porém, tendo em consideração a possibilidade de vir a realizar operações desta natureza mas com prazos superiores a cinco dias, o Director Financeiro do Banco pretende confirmar se tais operações podem igualmente beneficiar da referida isenção.

ao.title: Como saber se uma recuperação está a funcionar | E quando deve terminar?
ao.description: Um plano de recuperação deve, portanto, conter não apenas medidas para recuperar, mas também mecanismos para verificar se a recuperação está a acontecer. Se os resultados esperados não forem alcançados, é necessário perguntar se ainda existe viabilidade económica e qual a solução que melhor preserva o valor remanescente.
